name: Kalshi Taker Herding
description: Tested whether one-sided bursts of Kalshi taker buying overshoot (and can be faded) on the thin ETH/SOL 15-minute markets. They don't: net taker flow over the last 1-10 minutes has no predictive power for the outcome beyond the price, and fading or following it loses about the fee plus spread.
hypothesis: On thin books a burst of one-sided Kalshi taker buying walks the price beyond what spot justifies (retail chasing, quoters stepping back) and drifts back; net signed taker flow over the last few minutes should predict y - mid with a negative sign. Wrong if corr(imbalance, y - mid) isn't consistently signed in both halves, or the extreme imbalance quintile isn't positive at next real fills after fee in both halves on ETH or SOL.
next: Rejected at research (corr -0.02..+0.005 at W=60/180/600 s; fade negative in every quintile, both halves, all coins).
